failures.why: On a voice-first call with no keyboard, teacher told the child to select from on-screen buttons instead of answering by voice.

failures.quote: 8 mein kitne aur milaayein to 10 banega?
failures.why: Asked the same 8-partner question two turns in a row after the child had already answered it correctly.

failures.quote: Bilkul, tumne sahi pairs bataye.
failures.why: Treated the child’s correct button tap as proof the misconception was gone, though the child still believed only 5+5 was the real 10.

failures.quote: Bilkul, tumne sahi pairs bataye. Numbers swap karne par total kyun nahi badalta?
failures.why: After the child picked the right option, teacher assumed the misconception was resolved and jumped ahead to commutativity.

failures.quote: Numbers swap karne par total kyun nahi badalta?
failures.why: Moved to order/swap before confirming the child actually accepted that pairs other than 5+5 make 10.

failures.quote: Ab aage kya karenge? Count the folded fingers: ___.
failures.why: The same fill-in-the-blank screen was shown twice more unasked after its first use, mismatched to a voice-only interaction.

failures.quote: Count the folded fingers
failures.why: Checked the same folded-fingers count three times rapidly, annoying the child and breaking flow.

failures.quote: Tumne 3 aur 7 ka pair poocha; ab 3 ungliyan, phir 7 ungliyan gino.
failures.why: Responded to the child’s explicit confusion about 3+7 with yet another finger-counting routine instead of clarifying the concept.

judged2.verdict: Teacher made Gauri repeat the same finger count too many times, ignored when she got tired, and never really cleared her belief that only 5 and 5 make the 'real' 10.
